Define a Controlled Reasoning Task
Restrict proofs to chained modus ponens
Require one unique gold proof
Keep sentences easy to parse

Generate a Linear Ontology
Sample 3 to 10 concepts from a prior
Add subtype relations and properties
Give each node at most one child

Choose the Ontology Condition
Fictional concept names
Real-world-consistent true ontologies
Random counterfactual false ontologies

Seed a Formal Proof
Choose a starting node uniformly
Assign one entity to that concept
Create the initial logical axiom

Traverse Up the Ontology
Apply one deduction rule per hop
Stop at the target node or property
Control 1 · 3 · 5 proof hops

Render the Natural-Language Context
Map every edge and property by grammar
Use syntactically simple variants
Preserve a unique inverse parse

Control Context Difficulty
Add distractors to block shortcuts
Order facts top-down or bottom-up
Expose planning rather than retrieval

Create Query and Binary Label
State the proof's initial entity fact
Ask about conclusion or negation at 0.5
Label the item True or False

Generate the Gold Chain of Thought
Translate each proof conclusion
Keep one sentence per formal step
Store context · query · CoT · label

Run Eight-Shot CoT Evaluation
Generate demonstrations independently
Append one test question without answer
Decode the model's CoT and label

Parse Predicted CoT Symbolically
Apply the same simple grammar in reverse
Use recursive-descent semantic parsing
Recover a sequence of logical forms

Classify Every Proof Step
Test strict or broad validity
Test atomic versus skipped deductions
Mark correct path · misleading · invalid

Compare with the Gold Proof
Check whether the conclusion is reached
Compare the predicted binary label
Separate local from planning errors

Report Formal Reasoning Metrics
Label accuracy · strict proof accuracy
Skip · broad · valid proof accuracy
Break down by hops order and ontology
